entities.name: Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFLC or AFDL, Alliance des forces démocratiques pour la libération du Congo-Zaïre), founded in 1996 and led by Laurent-Désiré Kabila — was the rebel movement that overthrew Mobutu Sese Seko's 32-year dictatorship in the Democratic Republic of Congo (then Zaire), ending one of Africa's most notorious kleptocratic regimes in the First Congo War (1996-1997) with the crucial military support of Rwanda and Uganda.

The ADFLC's 1996-1997 military campaign — which swept from eastern Congo across the entire country in approximately seven months, covering one of the largest territories in Africa — was made possible primarily by Rwandan military support. Rwanda's new Tutsi-led government (post-1994 genocide) had strong motivation to pursue the Hutu interahamwe génocidaires who had fled into eastern Congo after the genocide, and the ADFLC's campaign served as cover for Rwanda's military objectives. This Rwandan military support, along with Ugandan assistance, was the real military force behind the ADFLC's extraordinary swift conquest.

Laurent-Désiré Kabila became President of the DRC in 1997 but proved as disappointing as Mobutu in many respects — quickly falling out with his Rwandan backers (triggering the Second Congo War in 1998, one of Africa's most catastrophic conflicts, killing approximately 5 million people directly and indirectly). Kabila was assassinated in 2001 and succeeded by his son Joseph Kabila. The ADFLC's overthrow of Mobutu thus led not to a genuine democratic transformation but to another authoritarian regime and an even worse war.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The ADFLC — which overthrew Mobutu's 32-year Zairian dictatorship but led to the catastrophic Second Congo War killing approximately 5 million people — is historically significant as a turning point in central African history whose consequences include Africa's deadliest modern conflict.
